text:
Sophia: quick note — hit a small but repeatable liveness hole with prefix eviction + demote. Node A demoted prefix X, node B still serving until its token expired, then a short window where reads returned 503. repro attached in logs below.

Mike: can you paste the log snippet or the minimal repro steps?

Sophia: sure, pasted the relevant tail here:
```
I0323 14:01:12.123 prefix=0x1a evict: mark-demote req_id=abcd lease=42 -> sending demote-commit
I0323 14:01:12.125 nodeB read ok prefix=0x1a req=fn123 lease=42
I0323 14:01:12.128 demote-commit acked on A -> token dropped
I0323 14:01:12.129 nodeB read hits missing-token -> 503
```
Looks like nodeB's in-memory view still believed it could serve for that tiny interval but the serve path checks token presence after the lease dropped.

James: that matches what I saw in a test harness last week. Race between demote-commit and token invalidation propagation. eviction token drop isn't synchronous across peers.

Tom: two ideas: (1) make demote a two-phase op: pre-reserve -> propagate -> final-commit, where pre-reserve keeps a short grace window during which both nodes treat the prefix as "read-only" (serve reads but not writes), or (2) on token drop, instead of immediate hard 503, serve a cached-stale-with-warning for up to N ms while we reconcile.

Anna: I prefer (1). It gives a clear consistency boundary. Stale reads risk confusing clients. Pre-reserve could be a lightweight lease extension on the current owner + a short quarantine TTL that followers observe.

Mike: +1 for pre-reserve/quarantine. Implementation trade: do we piggyback pre-reserve on the existing lease system (cheap) or add a separate demote-token with its own epoch (safer but more complexity)?

James: piggybacking seems easiest short-term: extend owner's demote-prelease by 200ms and have followers check demote-epoch before rejecting. We need metrics to validate.

Sophia: rough plan:
- add pre-reserve step to demote path that issues a demote-epoch bump and returns a short TTL (configurable, default 200ms)
- followers treat demote-epoch > local as "quarantine": continue serving reads but mark metric and avoid serving any new pin/lease grants
- final-commit clears token and increments epoch again -> followers immediately transition to not-serving
- add unit tests + integration canary, and a small perf test for extra msg load

Tom: sounds good. Few questions: what about multi-node handoff where owner crashes mid-pre-reserve? we should have a fallback where followers time out the pre-reserve and then try an immediate takeover after TTL expiry.

Anna: agree, add a takeover path after TTL if no final-commit seen. That avoids permanent hangs. Also add a gauge for "quarantine-count" and an alert for >1% of reads hitting quarantine for >5m.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary image with tag "kv-demote-quarantine-pt1" will be pushed to canary cluster at 20:30 UTC.

Mike: I'll file a short RFC summary and link the PR. Assign to Sophia as owner. Can you add a tiny simulation to the repo to model different network skews? even 50ms tail can matter.

Sophia: will do. Opening PR in a bit and adding a simulation script under ./tools/evict-sim. I'll also add the logs and the minimal repro steps to the issue.

James: nice. once PR lands let's run the simulated churn with canary and validate no 503 spikes. If OK, roll to shadow then prod.

Sophia: thanks all. I'll post the PR link here when ready. :thumbsup:
